recognition: A Companies House letter or Gazette notice saying the registrar intends to strike the company off the register (compulsory strike-off, 'First Gazette notice'), usually because a confirmation statement or accounts are overdue.

facts_for_explanation.what_it_is: Companies House thinks the company is no longer trading because a document is overdue (often the confirmation statement or the accounts). It plans to remove ('strike off') the company from the register.
facts_for_explanation.what_happens: A notice is published in The Gazette. If nothing is done, the company is usually struck off about 2 months later and dissolved. A dissolved company's bank accounts are frozen and its money and property pass to the Crown.
facts_for_explanation.how_to_stop_it: File the overdue documents (for example the confirmation statement and any overdue accounts) as soon as possible. Once they are filed, Companies House normally stops the strike-off. A company can also object to the strike-off.
facts_for_explanation.what_you_need: The company number and the Companies House authentication code (a 6-character code sent to the registered office).
facts_for_explanation.service: Accounted4Tax can file the confirmation statement (and any overdue accounts) for the company. The fee is quoted first; the director's ID is checked before we start.

needs: director ID (photo ID, selfie with photo ID, proof of address, certificate of incorporation)
service.price: as per quote (confirmation statement £99 including the Companies House fee; overdue accounts per package prices)
